text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Some 70 percent of Romanians are willing to accept the hardships brought by reforms, a poll by the Independent Institute for Social Studies said.
- The state-run Romtelecom telephone operator plans to raise tariffs in September.
- Recent cuts in customs taxes for food imports affect Romania's meat processing sector, the paper says.
- Some 500 miners in the northern coalfield of Cavnic staged a one-day strike last Staurday, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romanian President Emil Constantinescu will meet his Ukrainian and Moldovan counterparts in July to discuss joint cooperation projects.
- Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan is quoted as saying bilateral trade between Romania and Turkey will reach $1 billion in the near future.
- Restructuring of the mining sector will be carried out in three stages, over the next two years, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A Romanian-Canadian joint venture plans to launch a project to extract gold from mine tailings.
- Water levels on the Prut and Arges rivers reached flooding levels, the paper says.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will go to Strasbourg on Tuesday for a European Christian Democrats' summit.
- The newspaper quotes Bucharest police sources as saying that two skeletons were unearthed during digs at the presidential Cotroceni palace.
- The newspaper says today's no-confidence debates in parliament will be purely technical, with no chance of the opposition unseating the government.
- The paper quotes World Jewish Restitution Organisation sources as saying that Hungary is Europe's first ex-communist country to pay pensions to World War Two Holocaust survivors.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- "Tragic weekend for the Russian embassy in Bucharest" --- newspaper reports on the death of a member of the Russian diplomatic staff who drowned in the Snagov Lake on Friday and a car accident in which the Russian consul and his wife were injured when their car left the road and struck a tree.
- The Romanian army chief of staff, General Constantin Degeratu, ordered a multi-layered "Pro-NATO" cake for his son's wedding party.
LIBERTATEA
- The newspaper quotes official data as showing that some 5.3 million Romanians are living in poverty.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
